chapter: Cab Calloway, Lunceford, Hampton and Armstrong, 1941-45
title: Air bases, Fort Huachuca and secret security
summary: Armed services flew the band to Arizona bases, where security kept them from seeing anything, and Jimmy Mundy wrote at Fort Huachuca.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Yeah, armed services. We were in California and went out to the airport, and they flew us to Tucson, Arizona -- from California. They flew us out to Tucson to do -- Then we had -- we had two dances. We had
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
Fort Huachuca?

Yeah. Well, we played Fort Huachuca. We was at Fort Huachuca for about two or three days. Fort Huachuca was where they had the -- That's a basic colored base there, right? That's where the -- I forget the name of the outfit that was there that was supposed to be the best in the country.
I forget the name of that outfit too. Yeah.

The Mills Brothers was in the Army -- they were in there. They were out there. Jimmy Mundy was in the Army. He was writing -- he had a great big room. In the meanwhile, Jimmy had a great big barrack (inaudible), he had a room and he had Paul Whiteman's picture all over the wall. He was writing and they would let him off
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
to go to rehearse. Paul Whiteman -- he'd fly to California to rehearse with Paul Whiteman and come back. But he was writing for the Army and, you know, doing benefits for the Army and Navy.
They didn't do any fighting or anything like that. They were there -- had the band and they were writing arrangements.
But the whole time he was in the Army out in Fort Huachuca, a lot of the guys went to Fort Huachuca.
I don't know whether the Davis Monahan Air Force Base was in Tucson at that time.
There's an air base down there -- Davis Monahan. And I don't know whether that's the base you're talking about.
No, I'm talking about the Ellington Air Field -- we played that. That was a very strict --
You see, a lot of those places we played -- those air bases -- we didn't see no more than what they wanted us to see.
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
We couldn't go -- We did a Coca-cola show from the Ellington Air Field out there. And we didn't go -- we couldn't walk across the street around anywhere unless we had someone with us, you know.
Why is that?

Well the security was so tight. Remember, this was the time they were building all these bombers -- I guess they were getting ready to bomb Japan at that time. I guess they had all these secret planes and things they were doing at the time. We were doing benefits for those soldiers, and everything. Because when we went to Tucson, they had out there somewhere -- some place out there in Texas, they had this big -- They had dug it out, and all we could see were these -- as we passed by, just the tip of the plane. We couldn't see none of the planes. We didn't see any of the ground. They backed us up to the auditorium and we went on the stage.
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
And when we got finished, we packed up and went right back into the trucks again, and they took us right back to the airplanes and flew us back to California.
Top secret (inaudible) and spooky.
Top secret. We did a lot of top secret things.
